title: Twin Peaks Season 2 Atlas
description: Structured extraction dataset for visualizing Twin Peaks Season 2 character relationships and plot development. Built from public episode guides and recap sources; no transcript text is reproduced.

nodes.name: Dale Cooper
nodes.notes: FBI special agent; Season 2 follows his recovery, Laura Palmer case resolution, suspension, Windom Earle conflict, and Black Lodge entry.

nodes.name: Harry S. Truman
nodes.notes: Twin Peaks sheriff and Cooper's closest local partner; his bond with Cooper anchors the investigation.

nodes.name: Albert Rosenfield
nodes.notes: FBI forensic specialist; repeatedly returns with decisive evidence on Laura, Maddy, Cooper's shooting, Windom Earle, and Josie.

nodes.name: Gordon Cole
nodes.notes: Cooper's FBI superior; later returns with information on Project Blue Book and reinstates Cooper.

nodes.name: Garland Briggs
nodes.notes: Major Briggs links the town story to Project Blue Book, Owl Cave, Windom Earle, and the White/Black Lodge mythology.

nodes.name: Windom Earle
nodes.notes: Former FBI agent and Cooper's ex-partner; arrives as the late-season antagonist seeking revenge and access to the Black Lodge.

nodes.name: Annie Blackburn
nodes.notes: Norma's sister; becomes Cooper's love interest and the target Earle uses to lure Cooper into the Black Lodge.

nodes.name: Caroline Earle
nodes.notes: Windom Earle's murdered wife and Cooper's former love; her memory explains Cooper and Earle's feud.

nodes.name: Laura Palmer
nodes.notes: Murdered teenager whose case still structures the first half of Season 2 through visions, diary fragments, and the killer reveal.

nodes.name: Leland Palmer
nodes.notes: Laura's father; white-haired, unstable, revealed as BOB's host and Laura/Maddy's killer before dying in custody.

nodes.name: Sarah Palmer
nodes.notes: Laura's mother; haunted by visions and later left to process Leland and Laura's deaths.

nodes.name: Maddy Ferguson
nodes.notes: Laura's cousin; her murder becomes the second major killing that exposes the Palmer/BOB truth.

nodes.name: BOB
nodes.notes: Malevolent possessing entity connected to Laura's murder, Leland, Maddy's murder, and the final Cooper cliffhanger.

nodes.name: MIKE / Phillip Gerard
nodes.notes: One-armed man/inhabited host whose withdrawal lets MIKE point Cooper toward BOB.

nodes.name: The Giant
nodes.notes: Visionary figure who gives Cooper clues and later returns during the Black Lodge mythology.

nodes.name: Man From Another Place
nodes.notes: Red Room/Lodge figure tied to Cooper's dream language and Season 2 finale imagery.

nodes.name: Ronette Pulaski
nodes.notes: Survivor of Laura's attack; her hospital attack and memory fragments remain part of the Laura case.

nodes.name: Donna Hayward
nodes.notes: Laura's friend; investigates Laura's secret life through Harold Smith and later the Tremond/Chalfont clue.

nodes.name: James Hurley
nodes.notes: Laura/Donna's love triangle figure; after the killer reveal he drifts into the Evelyn Marsh subplot.

nodes.name: Harold Smith
nodes.notes: Reclusive friend of Laura who holds her secret diary; his death and torn diary redirect the investigation.

nodes.name: Audrey Horne
nodes.notes: Ben Horne's daughter; rescued from One-Eyed Jack's, helps clear Cooper, then enters the Wheeler/Ghostwood/Miss Twin Peaks arcs.

nodes.name: Ben Horne
nodes.notes: Great Northern owner; tied to One-Eyed Jack's, arrested for Laura's murder, then spirals before turning to Ghostwood and Wheeler.

nodes.name: Jerry Horne
nodes.notes: Ben's brother and business accomplice; context node for Horne schemes.

nodes.name: John Justice Wheeler
nodes.notes: Businessman Ben brings in to help; forms a short romance with Audrey.

nodes.name: Jean Renault
nodes.notes: Jacques and Bernard's brother; blackmails Ben and targets Cooper during the Audrey/One-Eyed Jack's plot.

nodes.name: Blackie O'Reilly
nodes.notes: Madam at One-Eyed Jack's involved in Audrey's captivity.

nodes.name: Bobby Briggs
nodes.notes: Shelly's lover and Major Briggs's son; later works with Ben and reveals Hank shot Leo.

nodes.name: Shelly Johnson
nodes.notes: Leo's wife and Bobby's lover; handles Leo's home care and later survives his escape.

nodes.name: Leo Johnson
nodes.notes: Violent husband of Shelly; survives shooting, becomes incapacitated, escapes, and is later used by Windom Earle.

nodes.name: Hank Jennings
nodes.notes: Criminal husband of Norma; implicated in Leo's shooting and Packard/Josie plots.

nodes.name: Norma Jennings
nodes.notes: Double R owner; Annie's sister and Ed's longtime love.

nodes.name: Ed Hurley
nodes.notes: Married to Nadine and in love with Norma; their triangle resurfaces at season end.

nodes.name: Nadine Hurley
nodes.notes: Wakes believing she is a high-schooler, joins wrestling, dates Mike, then regains memory after head trauma.

nodes.name: Mike Nelson
nodes.notes: High-school boy who becomes involved with Nadine during her amnesiac return to school.

nodes.name: Lucy Moran
nodes.notes: Sheriff's station receptionist; chooses Andy as father of her baby during the Miss Twin Peaks arc.

nodes.name: Andy Brennan
nodes.notes: Deputy; comic-investigative thread with Dick and key clue work near the finale.

nodes.name: Dick Tremayne
nodes.notes: Lucy's other suitor; shares Little Nicky subplot and becomes part of the baby-father choice.

nodes.name: Little Nicky
nodes.notes: Orphan subplot connected to Andy and Dick; low-priority context node.

nodes.name: Josie Packard
nodes.notes: Packard widow; flees after the mill fire, is revealed as Cooper's shooter, and dies after the Eckhardt confrontation.

nodes.name: Catherine Martell
nodes.notes: Survives the mill fire, returns disguised, and contests Packard/Ghostwood control.

nodes.name: Pete Martell
nodes.notes: Catherine's husband; survives the mill fire and helps open Eckhardt's puzzle box.

nodes.name: Andrew Packard
nodes.notes: Presumed-dead Packard who resurfaces, reshaping Josie/Catherine/Eckhardt stakes.

nodes.name: Thomas Eckhardt
nodes.notes: Josie's former lover/enemy whose arrival triggers her final crisis.

nodes.name: Jonathan
nodes.notes: Eckhardt/Josie-associated enforcer; context node for the Packard threat.

nodes.name: Evelyn Marsh
nodes.notes: Wealthy woman who draws James into an off-town murder frame-up.

nodes.name: Malcolm Sloan
nodes.notes: Evelyn's accomplice/lover in the James frame-up subplot.

nodes.name: Dwayne Milford
nodes.notes: Town mayor; context for the Milford/Lana subplot.

nodes.name: Lana Milford
nodes.notes: Younger woman in the Milford subplot; low-priority context node.

nodes.name: Laura Palmer Case
nodes.notes: Season 2's first-half murder investigation; use as a hub instead of connecting every investigator directly to every clue.

nodes.name: Cooper Shooting / Giant Clues
nodes.notes: Cooper recovers from being shot and receives the Giant's clues: a supernatural frame for the remaining Laura investigation.

nodes.name: Packard Mill Fire Aftermath
nodes.notes: Fallout from the mill fire: Shelly and Pete survive, Catherine disappears, Josie flees, Leo is guarded.

nodes.name: Secret Diary / Harold Smith
nodes.notes: Donna and Maddy's attempt to retrieve Laura's diary from Harold; ends with Harold's death and diary damage.

nodes.name: One-Eyed Jack's Rescue
nodes.notes: Audrey's captivity and Cooper/Truman's unauthorized raid; later causes Cooper's FBI suspension.

nodes.name: Maddy Murder
nodes.notes: Second killing by Leland/BOB that lets Cooper connect the case spiritually and forensically.

nodes.name: Killer Reveal / Leland Death
nodes.notes: Cooper exposes Leland as BOB's host; BOB departs and Leland dies in custody.

nodes.name: Cooper Suspension
nodes.notes: FBI suspends Cooper after the One-Eyed Jack's raid, keeping him in Twin Peaks as Earle approaches.

nodes.name: Project Blue Book
nodes.notes: Air Force/Briggs research context connecting Owl Cave, the Lodges, and Windom Earle.

nodes.name: Briggs Disappearance
nodes.notes: Major Briggs vanishes in the woods and returns with no memory and a strange mark.

nodes.name: Windom Earle Chess Game
nodes.notes: Earle announces his revenge on Cooper through a deadly chess game.

nodes.name: Josie Revealed / Death
nodes.notes: Albert reveals Josie shot Cooper; her death after Eckhardt leaves Harry devastated and supernatural questions open.

nodes.name: Owl Cave Petroglyph
nodes.notes: Map-like symbol discovered by Cooper, Briggs, Truman, Andy and others; key to entering the Black Lodge.

nodes.name: White Lodge / Black Lodge Lore
nodes.notes: Late-season mythology explaining Earle's objective and Cooper's danger.

nodes.name: Miss Twin Peaks Pageant
nodes.notes: Earle targets the pageant and uses Annie as the gateway victim for the Black Lodge.

nodes.name: Black Lodge
nodes.notes: The extradimensional destination of Earle, Annie, Cooper, BOB, and the finale's cliffhanger.

nodes.name: Possessed Cooper Cliffhanger
nodes.notes: Final state of Season 2: Cooper returns, but BOB's reflection indicates possession or replacement.

nodes.name: Ghostwood Estates
nodes.notes: Development/business plot connecting Ben, Catherine, Packard power, and Audrey's protest.

nodes.name: Double R Diner
nodes.notes: Norma's diner; social hub and Annie's arrival point.

nodes.name: Twin Peaks Sheriff's Department
nodes.notes: Main investigation workspace for Cooper, Truman, Hawk, Andy, Lucy, and FBI visitors.

nodes.name: Great Northern Hotel
nodes.notes: Ben Horne's hotel and a recurring site for Cooper, One-Eyed Jack's business, and Laura-case clues.

nodes.name: Marsh Murder Frame-Up
nodes.notes: James is drawn into Evelyn and Malcolm's scheme around Jeffrey Marsh's death.

nodes.name: Lucy Baby Choice
nodes.notes: Lucy resolves the Andy/Dick baby-father triangle at the Miss Twin Peaks event.

nodes.name: Eckhardt Puzzle Box
nodes.notes: Eckhardt's final nested box/lockbox subplot with Andrew, Pete, and Catherine.
